The combined structure consists of subgrains of the γ and γ′ phases, showing misorientations of more than 5°, and individual recrystallized γ′-grains formed in the interdendritic regions (figure 3(a)).
The alloy contains 45% of the strengthening γ′ phase, the temperature of complete dissolution of the γ′-phase (Tcdγ′) is 1170◦C.

When the material is heated prior to quenching at a temperature 100 °C below Tcdγ′, a necklace structure is formed, and the degree of recrystallization increases to 5–15%; with the recrystallized grains 5–6 µm in size.

attributes.location: boundaries of recrystallized grains and polygonized grains

evidence.quote: Precipitates of the coarse γ′ phase particles can be observed at boundaries of recrystallized grains and polygonized grains (figure 4(a)).
Two types of γ′ phase particles are observed: coarse cube-shaped 100–150 nm particles and ultrafine 10–20 nm spherical particles.

When the material is heated prior to quenching at a temperature 100 °C below Tcdγ′, a necklace structure is formed, and the degree of recrystallization increases to 5–15%; with the recrystallized grains 5–6 µm in size.

After repeated deformation at a temperature in the two-phase field 70 °C below Tcdγ′ followed by an intermediate recrystallization annealings at Tcdγ′ and a final deformation of 30% at a temperature 80 °C below Tcdγ′ a non-recrystallized structure is formed in the IM alloy. This structure contains deformed grains in the range 150–250 µm with some evidence of the initial stages of recrystallization.

Electron microscope examination of the as-deformed PM alloys shows that they have mainly a polygonized structure, and regions exhibiting an increased dislocation density. The polygonized structure is characterized by a subgrain size of 0.3–10 µm.

Heat treatment at a temperature 80°C below Tcdγ′ followed by quenching and ageing results in an increase in the amount of recrystallization. The recrystallized grains increase in size to some extent, up to 3 µm, in comparison with those observed in the alloy after deformation. The polygonized structure becomes better defined (figure 4(b)), and a partially recrystallized necklace-type structure can be observed.
Heat treatment of the PM alloy, followed by quenching from a temperature 10 °C above Tcdγ′ and ageing results in formation of a fine-grained recrystallized structure, with a grain size of 30–50µm.

attributes.location: zones of large shear stresses localization

evidence.quote: The main problem which occurs in production of highly-alloyed superalloy semiproducts is their poor ductility. In the case of IM alloys, this is caused by structural and chemical inhomogeneities in the ingot; while in the case the PM alloys it results from formation of microporosity in zones of large shear stresses localization, occurring during deformation.
